title: SiST: Token Similarity and Sparsity Aware Optimization for Transformers on FPGA
problem: Transformer inference on resource-constrained FPGAs is expensive due to high computational cost in QKV generation, attention, and FFN modules.
motivation: Prior FPGA work focuses on attention computation, but QKV generation and FFN typically dominate overall cost; sparsity and token patterns offer optimization opportunities.
method: SiST cuts unnecessary work in three places: it predicts which tokens can be skipped before generating QKV matrices (the Query, Key, and Value tensors used by attention), groups similar tokens in the FFN (the feed-forward layer) to share computations, and exploits weight sparsity by skipping calculations on near-zero weights. The FPGA is designed to handle this unstructured sparsity—where zeros are scattered randomly rather than in regular patterns—efficiently.
key_novelty: The core innovation is co-designing the transformer algorithm and FPGA hardware together as a single system to exploit both token similarity and weight sparsity across all three transformer modules (QKV generation, attention, and FFN).
limitations: Accuracy loss <2% but not detailed per-layer; cross-stage sparsity prediction requires offline weight clustering.
primary_theme: Sparsity and token similarity optimization for FPGA transformers
